t: A son of Huayna Cápac who spent his youth campaigning with his father in the north, Atahualpa governed Quito under his half-brother Huáscar until their rivalry broke into civil war in 1529.
His generals Quizquiz, Chalcuchímac and Rumiñawi won the war in April 1532, capturing Huáscar and seizing Cusco, just as Francisco Pizarro's small Spanish force was marching inland.

Seized in an ambush at Cajamarca in November 1532, he offered a room of gold and silver for his life, but the Spaniards tried him for revolt, idolatry and Huáscar's murder and garroted him in 1533 after his baptism.
dyk: The Quechua word wallpa for 'chicken' was long thought to explain Atahualpa's name; since the bird was new to the Andes, scholars now think it more likely the bird was named after him, as Blas Valera said in the 16th century.
ev: Born a son of the Inca emperor Huayna Cápac, in Cusco by the most trusted chronicles, though other accounts place his birth near Quito
Relations with Huáscar have broken down, and the two brothers begin the Inca Civil War over the succession
Francisco Pizarro lands on Puná Island with 180 men and 37 horses and hears of the civil war
His generals defeat Huáscar's army at Quipaipán in April, capture Huáscar and seize Cusco
Captured in November in an ambush on the square at Cajamarca, where the Spaniards kill a great number of his retinue
Condemned by a trial staged by Pizarro, baptised to escape burning and executed by garrote

f.born: c. 1502, place disputed: Cusco by the chroniclers Cieza de León and Betanzos, Caranqui or Quito by other accounts and by his own statement before his death; son of the emperor Huayna Cápac
f.died: 1533 at Cajamarca, garroted by the Spaniards after a trial that sentenced him to be burned; the date is given both as 26 July and as 29 August
f.role: Governor of Quito under Huáscar; leader of the northern side in the Inca Civil War (1529–1532); Sapa Inca from April 1532, with the regnal name Caccha Pachacuti Inca Yupanqui Inca; a prisoner of the Spaniards from November 1532
f.known: the Inca Civil War against Huáscar; the victory at Quipaipán and the taking of Cusco; his capture in the ambush at Cajamarca; the room he offered to fill with gold and silver; his trial and execution; the Inkarri myth of his return
